hypothesis: A single-process search that builds the pinned circle B cache once and evaluates candidates sequentially will remain stable on the current WSL host, identify strong n=7 candidates, and permit at least one exact full circle-taxi evaluation without the cache duplication that broke the prior staged pipeline.
rationale: The prior three k-server staged configurations all failed during worker initialization. Direct memory inspection found that the n=7 circle cache is approximately 1001 x 279936 int32, about 1.12 GB per process; concurrent fast workers therefore duplicate the dominant allocation. This experiment changes the runtime architecture to one shared cache and sequential candidate evaluation while preserving the pinned matrix, candidate coefficient family, primary metric, and upstream evaluator logic.
expected_information_gain: Separates a mathematical/search failure from the measured cache-duplication runtime failure. A stable run with completed exact taxi scoring reopens the documented search path; instability or inability to build the one-process cache provides a clean capability boundary.
method: Load the exact pinned search source at commit aea64346b846c967e4448f098d4b8b1748504d27 and reuse its build_ck4_cache, mutate_vector, evaluate_ck4_cached, Potential, and evaluate_heavy_candidate functions without changing the matrix or scoring logic. Build one complete circle cache in the main process. For at most 600 seconds, generate deduplicated vectors from the pinned seed_dense, seed_sparse, mutate_ck4, mutate_proxy, mutate_timed, and mutate_full families; evaluate every vector exactly on all 6006 circle edges; retain the best circle candidates. Then load the pinned circle-taxi metric and run the unmodified full stage-D candidate evaluator sequentially with one nested potential process on the best two circle candidates or until the 1200-second wall budget expires. Preserve all counts, vectors, timings, errors, and artifact hashes.
metric: primary: exact circle_taxi_k4_m6 violations_k for each completed full evaluation; capability diagnostics: cache construction, completed circle candidates, best circle violations, and full-evaluator coverage
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A completed candidate with violations_k < 3 on the pinned circle-taxi metric is finite benchmark progress toward the k-server objective, not a proof of the full conjecture. Circle-only scores and partial runs are runtime/search diagnostics and cannot establish the target.

configuration.cache_architecture: one in-process circle B cache; no fast worker pool

compute_budget.cpu: one search process plus one nested potential process during sequential taxi evaluation

kill_condition: Stop at the first completed exact taxi result below 3, at 1200 seconds, or at a precise cache/runtime/contract failure. Do not modify protected evaluator code or infer mathematical infeasibility from a failed capability run.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if exact evaluator returns violations_k < 3; reproduction at 3 is baseline evidence

previous_best_comparison.previous_pipeline_result: three worker configurations failed before completed scoring
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: shared-cache architecture must first demonstrate completed exact scoring

repetition_justification: This is not another worker-count reduction. It removes the fast worker pool entirely, builds the circle cache once, and evaluates the candidate stream sequentially, directly addressing the measured approximately 1.12GB-per-process cache duplication that caused pipeline-003 through pipeline-005 to fail before scoring.
